message.content: Four people on my street have each bought a tile cutter they used once. I want to fix that, but every version of it I imagine collapses the moment someone moves away.
The collapsing is the interesting part. Before we design the lending: who is it for, what happens when something comes back broken, and where do the tools actually live?

description: Three insights standing at the far end of the board while a question in the middle row is still open. This is the whole argument for ungating: under the old rule this corner was a dashed ring, because a conclusion was withheld until every row was finished. One of the three says on its face that it was written before the person's last two answers, and the row holding the open question still draws its line to the stack — because it fed it.
